entries.etymology_notes: Preverbal future tense particle developed as an apocopic contraction of the active participle sejjer (going to), with historical substrate analogy to Arabic sa-.

definitions.text_mt: Partiċella preverbjali li tindika ż-żmien futur jew intenzjoni immedjata li titwettaq azzjoni.

usage_examples.mt: Għada se mmorru l-baħar kmieni.
usage_examples.en: Tomorrow we will go to the sea early.

usage_examples.en: The doctor will arrive in a few more minutes.

alternative_forms.notes: Variant found in older texts and some regional dialects

entries.audit_notes: Refined to Il-Miġma and Oxford lexicographical standard. Tautology eliminated; etymology updated to reflect participle apocope of sejjer.

entries.etymology_notes: From Arabic wa-kull (and all, as well).

entries.audit_notes: Refined to Il-Miġma standard. Replaced placeholder definition with functional additive phrasing.

entries.audit_notes: Refined to Il-Miġma standard.

entries.etymology_notes: Grammaticalized imperative from the verb żied (to add), used as an arithmetic operator.

entries.audit_notes: POS aligned to preposition. Definition refined to mathematical operation standard.

entries.etymology_notes: From Arabic hâhunâ (here, in this place).

definitions.text_mt: F'dan il-post jew f'din il-pożizzjoni fejn jinsab il-kelliem.

entries.etymology_notes: From Arabic barran (outside, outwards), adverbial accusative of barr (open country, land).

usage_examples.mt: Ħarġu jilagħbu barra fil-ġnien nazzjonali.

entries.etymology_notes: Adverbial compound formed from darba (time, occasion) and oħra (other, fem.).

definitions.text_mt: F'okkażjoni oħra jew fi żmien li għad irid jiġi; mill-ġdid.

entries.etymology_notes: From Arabic fatīt (fragment, crumb). Functions adverbially to indicate limited degree, quantity, or time.

definitions.text_mt: Fi kwantità żgħira, fi grad limitat jew għal tul ta' ħin qasir; mhux wisq.

usage_examples.mt: Stenna ftit sakemm inlesti x-xogħol.

entries.audit_notes: ID normalized from adj- to adv- for adverbial entry. Definition refined to adverbial usage.

entries.etymology_notes: From Arabic bas (only, enough), borrowed from Persian bas (enough, only).

definitions.text_mt: B'mod uniku, esklużivament u mingħajr żieda ta' xejn jew ħadd aktar.

entries.etymology_notes: From Arabic ħafnaẗ (handful), grammaticalized into a degree adverb and quantifier.

usage_examples.mt: Ħadmu ħafna biex ilestu l-proġett fil-ħin.

usage_examples.mt: Poġġi l-kaxxa hawnhekk fuq il-mejda biex ma taqax.
usage_examples.en: Put the box right here on the table so it doesn't fall.

entries.etymology_notes: Spoken emphatic form of hawn with terminal paragogic vowel -a.

definitions.text_en: right there, over there, in that exact place
